Header: Obereopsis brevis Vernacular name: Chakri Bhunga

Prevention: Used broad base furrow technology for sowing.
Remove alternate host plants from the field e.g.
Larger plant populations result in increased infestation.
Monitoring: Infestation starts from 18-21 days after sowing.
Stem tissues are eaten by larvae, which results in tunnelling.
Girdling of stems causes drying of shoots and branches
Direct Control: Manual collection and destruction of infested plant parts.
Application of neem seed kernel extract 5% as a repellent for egg laying.
